spell.name: Numbering the Flock
spell.text:
The Numerologist instantly knows the number of animals she can see, and how many of each kind.

The pattern of such numbers is considered to be far more significant than the details of the numbers. Numerologists often use this spell in connection with Casual Augury (Numerology) to interpret the numbers.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (InAn)

spell.name: Shearing the Unseen Sheep
spell.text:
Creates a sheep's fleece. Wool is the most common material for making clothing, but creating ready-made woolen garments

is difficult with Hermetic Magic. As a consequence, Julia uses this spell to create the raw materials, and then rearranges them into clothing using Rego Craft Magic, such as *Woolen Garments for the Human Form*, below.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: The Welcome Addition of False Sunlight
spell.text: This spell creates a steady, cool, smokeless light that does not flicker. Variants of this spell are enchanted into devices in many libraries. Some are handheld, while others float by their user, are embedded in the ceiling, or overlook the work desks of individual scholars.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: Step Sideways
spell.text: The caster instantly moves to a location she can see within 50 paces. If a Dexterity + Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is failed, then something goes slightly awry: she might be facing the wrong way, or appears a foot or two above the ground.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: Seal the Earth
spell.text: Creates enough dirt to fill in a pit of up to 6 paces across and 3 paces deep.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: Palm of Hearing
spell.target: Hearing The caster can hear from the perspective of the target. This spell must Penetrate in order to sense creatures with Magic Resistance. Ariane has learned this spell to cast down an Intangible Tunnel

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: Black Anne's Kiss
spell.text: This spell wounds an unborn child, causing the fetus to abort. A Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 6 must be made for the mother; if it fails she suffers a Medium Wound.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: Smoke of Escaping
spell.target: Individual Creates the illusion of a thick cloud of red smoke in the caster's vicinity
spell.design: Base 1, +1 Touch, +1 Diameter, +1 size, +1 impenetrable to sight

spell.name: Inscribe the Line

spell.design: Base 2, +2 Sun, +2 affect metal; +1 for 2/day, +3 triggered by sunrise/set

spell.name: Clear Sight of the Naiad

spell.name: Sense the Weight of Divine Power
spell.text: This rote (designed using the Hermetic Numerology Mystery Virtue) is a simple effect to tell the caster what strength of Divine aura he is currently standing in.

spells.why: asked for: Intellego, Creo, Animal, Terram, Corpus

spell.name: The Racing Rot

A Perception + Finesse roll determines the skill with which the previous writing has been removed.

spell.name: Wall of Living Wood
spell.text: A straight wall of living oak is created, growing quickly from nearby trees, other plant growth, or fertile earth. The wall is 20 paces long, 1 pace thick, and 5 paces high. It can be scaled with a Dexterity + Athletics stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrHe)

spell.name: Trap of the Entwining Vines
spell.text: Causes strong, woody vines to grow rapidly from fertile earth. The vines cover a circle 2 paces across and reach 6 feet high. Anything caught within them is immobilized. To avoid the vines, the target must make a Quickness — Encumbrance stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9. To break out requires a Strength stress roll against an Ease Factor of 12 (allowed once a round). Someone not trapped can cut a trapped person free in two rounds, assuming proper tools. The vines weaken and wither to dust at sunrise or sunset.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrHe)

spell.name: Rising Ire
spell.text: Makes the target furious at someone or something of your choice. A stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 using an appropriate Personality Trait (like Calm) can hold the anger in check, but it is felt strongly regardless of the roll.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrMe)

spell.name: Look at Me
spell.text: This spell creates a thought in the imagination of the target, causing him to look directly at the caster even if the caster has not been previously noticed by the target. This glance is sufficient to make eye contact. If concentrating on another task, the target may make a Stamina + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 6 to resist. This spell is most often cast with no voice or gestures as a subtle way of attracting someone's attention.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrMe)

spell.name: Zephaniah's Brazier
spell.text:
This brazier is a copper dish about five inches in diameter. The color of the smoke in the brazier can be used to determine whether an individual is dead. To use the brazier it is lit, and the name of the target is spoken into the white smoke spiraling upwards from the dish. If the individual is dead, the smoke changes, becoming acrid and purple in color. The brazier may be used once per day.

(Effect: Base 4, +3 Veil)

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: The Unseen Porter
spell.text: Like *Unseen Arm* (ReTe 5), but it can carry large objects such as crates. Roughly speaking, it has the capabilities of a very strong person (Str +5). The heavier the object is, the slower the unseen porter moves. If delicacy is required, high Finesse stress rolls (Ease Factor 12 or so) are needed. The spell can only carry inanimate objects, and cannot carry you. It also cannot lift things more than 6 feet above the ground. Casting requisites of an appropriate Form for the target are required.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Distraction of the Magpie
spell.text: The target's estimation is altered so that shiny objects become highly desirous to him. For the duration of the spell he is easily distracted by anything that glints, and given the opportunity he will acquire such things and secret them somewhere about his person. He must make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to complete a complex task in the presence of a shiny object that he does not yet possess.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Warning Flame
spell.target: Individual This wand ignites a brazier at the end of
spell.text:
the Sacred Way (just outside the Aegis of the Hearth). The wand is carried by Callista and she lights the brazier to signal to the covenant that there is an emergency in Miletos.

When the brazier ignites, the covenfolk find a magus for assistance. Usually Ariane is the most useful as she can easily open an Intangible Tunnel to question Callista.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: The Apprentice's Delight
spell.text: This spell creates a ripe apple that lasts for two minutes, long enough to be gobbled down. The apple provides no nourishment; its pleasure is in the sweetness of eating it.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie
spell.text: For as long as you maintain this spell, the target exhales a misty breath with each spoken lie. Small bits of ice form on the person's lips if the lie is particularly severe. In winter, when breath is visible anyway, lies produce a greater than normal amount of mist (the mist actually billows out). A target who makes a Communication + Guile stress roll against an Ease Factor of 15 can determine whether any given statement will be taken by the spell as a lie. The spell can be defeated through extensive and judicious application of Creo Auram and Perdo Auram spells, and a demon is able to manipulate it in any way it wishes, as demons are the embodiment of deception and are never caught in a lie if they do not wish to be. House Guernicus brought the Order this spell, and it is a very poor Quaesitor who is without it.
spell.design: Base 10, +1 Eye, +1 Conc, mist is a purely cosmetic effect and thus is free

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Dust Devil of Auram Vis
spell.text:
This small whirlwind of Auram vis provides a constant breeze of fresh air that keeps the air breathable even in an airtight room. The Auram vis may only be transported with magic or in a hermetically sealed container.

(Effect: Base 1, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 unnatural; Modifications +1 2 uses per day, +3 environmental trigger)

**Mistletoe Sprig of Herbam Vis**

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Create the Flowers of the Moon
spell.text: Decorates a room with fresh flowers that grow normally and require care and watering. The quality of the floral display is determined by a Finesse roll. The flowers persist until the spell expires, then simply cease to exist.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Concoct Cordage
spell.text: The attached vine grows an additional ten feet per activation.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: The Magic Flute
spell.text:
This spell conjures a carved wooden flute into the hands of the caster. The flute appears just as the caster wishes, although casting requisites are required for flutes decorated with materials belonging to forms other than Herbam, such as the animal horn often used for embellishments.

Having only Concentration Duration, the flute is entirely magical and will disappear at the end of the spell's duration, essentially when Yestin finishes playing it. Yestin benefits from his Performance Magic Virtue when casting this spell, as the act of playing the flute stands in for his concentration.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Securing the Harvest
spell.text: This ward prevents any mundane pest from entering and absconding with the food growing within the protective boundary of the circle. If Maris finds that the ward has been bypassed and the food tampered with, it is an indication that something far more interesting than vermin has been in the area.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Herbam, Mentem, Vim

spell.name: Grow the Bountiful Feast
spell.text:
This spell ensures that all plants within

the circle grow healthily, and produce a good crop. The plants still mature normally, but when it comes time to harvest, all will produce the maximum amount of crops, of the finest quality the plant can produce.

spell.name: Bed of Rapid Convalescence
spell.text: A leather sick-bed engraved with Creo and Corpus runes, as well as symbols of Apollon, the Greek god of healing. Anyone resting in this bed receives a +18 bonus to his recovery rolls, as long as he remains in the bed for the whole of the recovery period. Aurulentus created this item as a lesser enchanted device.
spell.design: Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 level 2 uses/day, +3 levels environmental trigger

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrCo)

spell.name: Potion of Creation
spell.text:
When a fertile woman drinks this potion she is guaranteed to conceive if she has intercourse with a fertile man within a day. If the man is not human (a faerie, for example), then the woman still conceives if a stress roll plus her Stamina succeeds against an Ease Factor of 9; such a child inherits some traits from his father.

(Effect: Base 15, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; Modifications: None)

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrCo)

spell.name: Arc of Fiery Ribbons
spell.text: A dozen multi-hued ribbons of flame leap from your hands and fly out as far as your voice carries, covering a 60-degree arc. All those in the arc take +10 damage.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrIg)

spell.name: Lamp without Flame
spell.text: This spell creates a steady light as bright as daylight on a cloudy day. The light has no apparent source, but illuminates an area about ten paces across, centered on a point indicated by the caster. This point may be a mobile item.

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrIg)

spell.name: Box of Stone
spell.text:
When this effect is triggered, the floor, walls, and ceiling of the room containing the enchanted device are covered by a foot of stone. This stone interposes itself between the contents of the room and the walls, floor, and ceiling. The Pebble of the Stone Prison is deployed resting against a wall or the floor of a room so the created stone walls interpose themselves between the device and the targets that the designers hoped to catch. Objects affixed to the outside of the rooms such as tapestries and rugs end up outside of the stone. Objects resting on the floor or walls, such as people, tables, or tapestries, are pushed a foot toward the center of the room by the stone. Creatures and objects with Magic Resistance are not pushed by the stone box; rather the box grows around them and is created with holes at the locations of the protected creatures or objects.

This stone box is self-supporting and will not collapse under its own staggering weight, but the environment must be able to support it. Therefore, this justiciar can only be safely employed in a few rooms on the foundation level of Coeris without triggering a collapse of the building. Hermanus's use of this device in his laboratory was unwise, but he was overwhelmed by paranoia by the time he set it up. Fortunately, it was not triggered before the laboratory was ripped into the Twilight Void, and the room is now resting on the seabed.

(Effect: Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 size; Modifications, +1 level 2 uses per day)

spells.why: from: your strongest Arts (CrTe)

spell.name: Note These Landmarks
spell.text: At the wielder's verbal command, the stylus scribes markings onto the wax tablet that describe distances and landmarks sufficient to make the map of the regio boundary navigable. The stylus understands a set of Latin words, primarily numbers and distances, such as "twenty paces" or "thirteen feet", and landscape features, such as "tree" or "door" and is able to form symbols to match. This effect can be used while the stylus is inscribing a regio boundary without damaging the map.
spell.design: Base 2, +2 affect metal; +10 for unlimited use

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Eyes of the Fish
spell.text: The target gains the eyes of a fish, which allow him or her to see clearly while underwater but only blurrily while out of the water.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Tremulous Vault of the Torch's Flame
spell.text: Causes a fire to guiver a few seconds and then make a leap of up to 10 feet in any direction. A Targeting roll is required to hit a specific target. The flame stays at the spot it hits if it can burn there (see rules for fire damage on page 407). Otherwise, it simply scorches the spot and goes out (doing +5 damage).

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: The Mended Tear
spell.text: The caster lays a piece of linen or cotton thread over a rent in any fabric and runs her finger over it; the cloth or leather is immediately repaired with a neat stitch. This Craft Magic spell requires successful Finesse roll against an Ease Factor of 6.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Blind the Insurgent Pack
spell.text: Black, oily tears appear in the eyes of all individuals of the affected Group, burning and blurring their vision. With their eyesight blurred, and all sources of light reduced to unrecognizable sparkles, affected targets are considerably hindered while performing actions that depend on eyesight. They are subject to a –3 penalty to all rolls that involve sight (see Poor Eyesight Flaw, **ArM5**, page 58). If left to themselves, the victims' blurred vision heals as a Light Wound.
spell.design: Base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Group, free cosmetic effect

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Well without Light
spell.text: Removes light from the target structure. Only spells greater than level 25 can create light within this area. When casting this spell, magi typically clench a hand into a fist, and the light flows into the fist like a living entity, until the entire area is dark.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Circle of Eternal Spring
spell.text: This spell ensures that all plants within the circle grow well. It has the same effect as *The Bountiful Feast* (**ArM5**, page 135), but is based on Ring Duration and Circle Target.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Saving the Apprentice's Time
spell.text: Realizing she could squeeze in a few more precious moments of lab time, Conscentia decided to "cheat" in her chores. With just a wave of the hand, she can have an hour's worth of dusting completed in a minute.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: Soothe the Ferocious Bear
spell.text: Calms an animal until it is threatened or aroused again. You must speak soothingly or musically to it, and something as simple as approaching it may arouse it again.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

spell.name: The Welcome Stranger
spell.text:
This spell inserts a recollection of the caster into the target's memory. The memory itself soon fades, but its fleeting presence is usually enough to reassure the target that he has met the caster before.

The nature and context of the memory is determined when the spell is cast.

Even fond or favorable memories are not enough to counteract the effects of The Gift, but the guidelines in **ArM5**, page 76, give an idea how the memory of an established relationship influences behavior.

In later years, Yestin mastered this spell such that he can cast it both quietly and without the normal Hermetic gestures.

spells.why: asked for: Creo, Rego, Corpus, Ignem, Terram

library.title: Lab Text: Brilliance of the Eagle's Plumage
library.author: Servius of Bonisagus
library.subject: Brilliance of the Eagle's Plumage

spell.name: Brilliance of the Eagle's Plumage
spell.text: Anyone looking directly at the caster is blinded by the brilliant light shining from his body. The caster does not shed light as such; it is only those who look at him who are affected. All victims must make a Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to avoid blindness. On a botch, the blinding is permanent, otherwise a Stamina stress roll (no botch) against an Ease Factor of 9 can be attempted every minute until recovered.

library.title: Lab Text: Strings of the Unwilling Marionette
library.author: Lucanus of Flambeau
library.subject: Strings of the Unwilling Marionette

spell.name: Strings of the Unwilling Marionette
spell.text: You can control the physical movements of a person, such as walking, standing, and turning. If the target resists the control, the movements are jerky. The target can yell, but you can prevent intelligible speech by controlling the target's mouth. The target must be conscious to be moved about.

spell.name: Ward against Wood
spell.text: The caster is protected from nonenchanted wood, so that none of it can contact his body. If he is walking on a wooden surface, he is actually suspended very slightly above it.
